title: Focal Length
description: Lying on the pavement between towers, looking straight up. Turn the zoom ring from 24 mm to 10 mm: at the long end it is mostly cumulus, the towers creeping in at the corners; as it widens they lean in from the edges and the corners stretch like a real rectilinear ultra-wide, and below 16 mm the drawing eases toward stereographic so the towers bend into spokes round the sky. The camera never moves, so nothing about the perspective changes, only how much of it the lens takes in and how it is drawn. One 360 capture, projected exactly through r = f k tan(theta / k), developed like daylight negative film.
intent: Summer-film genre spec, idea 6 (Focal Length), adapted to a worm's-eye view: herb's reference 2 (factory/reality/herb-refs/2-wormseye-skyscrapers.png), towers converging into a cumulus sky, reached by turning a zoom ring rather than tilting. Projection family from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fisheye_lens#Mapping_function

sources.author: Andreas Mischok
sources.note: 16K HDR, the towers and street. Reprojected to a zenith cap (azimuthal equidistant, 95 degrees) and re-lit by the new sky's sun: facade normals from the floor lines give each face a sun incidence, sun-facing faces get about a stop of warm-neutral light, faces turned away go toward near-black with a little skylight blue, and cranes stay backlit silhouettes. Then regraded on the exported plates (regrade_towers.py) toward herb's ref 2: shade faces taken down 1.1 stops and tinted cobalt (212 degrees), their glass a mirror of what is across the street: each pane reflects, through a teal coating, about 30% of the plate in its mirror direction (the elevation kept, the azimuth mirrored in the face's normal, raised for the parallax of a ray that leaves the facade rather than the camera), so the crowns and the upper floors carry the cumulus and the lower ones the towers opposite, modulated by each pane's own texture; sun-facing faces lifted 0.7 stop under the clouds' own soft shoulder, with the sun map read from the faces' existing warmth; on them only the stone and the mullions take warm gold (35 to 38 degrees), while the glass, keyed from the capture's own cool chroma, keeps its grey-teal hue with some skylight mixed in, so teal glass and warm stone sit side by side. Last, clone_cap.py takes out three distractions: the crown of a distant tower that the 10 mm frame clipped into a floating fragment at its top edge (replaced with sky fitted to its surroundings), the lettering of a news ticker on the curved tower, and a crane jib floating in the sky past the stone tower's crown (inpainted from the clear sky round it). Then face_cap.py makes two clean-3D repairs on the curved glass tower at the lower left: its shaded flank, which the mirror pass had smeared into soft cloud blobs with a pale streak down the arris, is rebuilt from the native 16K capture sampled straight into each plate's geometry (area-averaged), so its mullion and floor grid carries on from the lit face at full sharpness, toned to the old flank's smooth profile in cobalt-teal; its arris is redrawn on the capture's own vertical edge and choked 2.5 px, with the uncovered strip filled from the clean sky beyond; and the rooftop and crane jib that poked in at the bottom-centre edge of the 10 mm frame become sky (a push-pull fill from the clear sky round them, with its own fine noise), ending past the frame on a roofline that never shows. Last, glass_faces.py gives the two towers right of the sky the same rebuild: the dark grid tower at right-middle and the curved glass tower above it, whose rounded crown and canopy span the top-right of the 14 and 20 mm frames, had taken the mirror pass as grey-blue blotches and smears that dissolved their window grid. Both are resampled from the native 16K capture straight into each plate's geometry (area-averaged), so the stone frame and window grid of the one and the structural fins of the other stay sharp all the way across; the body light is one smooth profile down each tower in the curved tower's flank cobalt, pulled toward teal, with the capture's pane texture compressed hard; and the glass carries one coherent mirror of the sky alone (the plate with its towers pushed out and filled from the sky round them), read in each face's mirror direction and weighted by Schlick Fresnel for that incidence, instead of per-pane reflections. The fins are kept as long ridges of the capture (a width-selective top-hat, small pieces dropped), and where the curved tower's glass reflects the grid tower opposite, only straight runs survive, so that reflection does not come back as a lattice. Last, canopy_glass.py rebuilds the curved tower's crown and canopy again, which that pass had left a flat slate card with scribbled curves: its fins are the capture's own ridges (a width-selective top-hat opened by long straight segments, so the reflected lattice and the tree drop out), lit with their own lit and shaded edges in a cool aluminium grey, and its glass carries no pane texture, only a smooth body light and one coherent Fresnel-weighted mirror of the sky: the crown's glass leans back as it rounds over, so it reflects the cumulus overhead, and each cell between the fins is a flat pane, so the reflection steps a little at every fin the way a curtain wall does. Even so it read as a flat CG card, so the piece no longer leans on it: the engine turns the cap 32 degrees about the zenith (ROLL, a quarter more on an upright frame), which puts that crown on the frame's short axis and mostly past its top edge, where only its nearest corner shows at 10 mm and a sliver at 14 mm. The dark grid tower and the gold stone tower now take the top corners, the curved stone tower and its lower neighbour the bottom right, so every edge carries a photographed facade. Last, topleft_tower.py rebuilds the top-left corner, which with that roll held the stub of the distant glass tower clone_cap.py had cut (a flat grey card off the top edge) and two blocks taken to near-black as shade faces, and was open sky at 14 mm: the card and the blocks become the plate's own sky, and a sunlit stepped stone tower from the same capture (the one at azimuth 86 to 113) stands there instead, moved as a rigid body (the same tower further off and standing lower, so its edges stay on their azimuths and run to the zenith, and its windows keep their shape) with its crown at rho 0.52, inside the 14 mm corner and short of the 20 mm one; its light is ranked onto the gold tower beside it, with that tower's colour at each rank, so its stone is gold and its glass grey-teal. Last, canopy_photo.py puts that curved glass tower's crown, whose railed corner still holds the top centre at 10 and 14 mm, back to the photograph: the native 16K capture holds its curtain wall together (a mullion and transom grid bending round the rounded corner, the railing band along its foot, and a coherent reflection of the grid tower across the street), so it is resampled straight into each plate's geometry (area-averaged) and only developed. Its log light is split into a large-scale body, compressed and set to the shade level of the towers round it, and the detail, kept whole, so every pane edge and the arris are the capture's; its colour is the rebuilt faces' cobalt-teal carrying the capture's own relative chroma, so aluminium stays greyer than glass, with the brightest reflections eased toward the plate's sky; and its edge is unmixed from the capture's own luminance, so the plate's sky shows through the railing. The street trees in front are re-cut from the native 16K capture (sky-unmixed coverage, kept where the foreground is green, or anything not sky round the tall conifer), so the canopy is a sharp silhouette, and the plate's alpha marks it: the engine develops those pixels without the film's diffusion, so the trees are the one crisp edge in the frame. Last, stone_flank.py gives the curved stone tower on the right of the 10 mm hero the same clean-3D rebuild: its shaded flank, which the mirror pass had covered in one grey-white smear per pane, is resampled from the native 16K capture straight into each plate's geometry (area-averaged), inside the shadow edge the plate already drew, so its stone frame, punched windows and the ribbon-glazed bay's transoms and mullions carry on from the sunlit floors at full sharpness. The stone takes one smooth cobalt profile down the tower with the capture's own joints; the glass (keyed by the capture's cool chroma, and in the bay, whose lower panes mirror the warm tower opposite, by the frame's own thin straight lines) takes one smooth cobalt body light plus one coherent mirror of the sky alone, read in each face's mirror direction and weighted by Schlick Fresnel, with the lamps and the news ticker's lettering taken out. The same pass turns the crane tip and white rooftop that poked above the gold tower's parapet at the left edge of the 10 mm frame into sky. Last, crown_cap.py cleans up the bottom centre and the left edge of the 10 mm hero: the two crane hooks and their hairline cables that hung in open sky over the small distant diagrid tower become sky (a push-pull fill from the clear sky round them, with its own fine noise); that tower, still being topped out in the capture, had come out with a torn, open-truss crown, so its roof line is found in the native 16K capture (a robust two-run fit along the parapet, the cranes dropped as outliers) and the crown band is resampled from the capture into the plate's geometry under it, its members drawn as the diagrid and the gaps closed as glass, with sky above; and its blown cream stone is ranked onto the sunlit gold tower's colour curve (luma by rank, chroma onto the gold's), keyed by the capture's own thin warm members so its glass stays cool teal glass. At the left edge the street trees' lowest twigs, which crossed into the frame as dark speckles, become sky and leave the crisp mask, and the pale grey-white strip of sky in the gap between the two gold towers is re-tinted onto a smooth fit of that gap's own clean cyan, keeping its texture.

sources.author: Greg Zaal (original), Jarod Guest (sky edits)
sources.note: 16K HDR cumulus sky, set in behind the towers with a luminance matte (sky at infinity, so the composite is geometrically exact), rotated so the sun sits behind a tower, and regraded as clear sky plus cloud light on a smooth, dithered ramp from cyan 200 degrees at the horizon to cobalt 212 degrees at the zenith, saturation capped so no gap goes ultramarine. The cumulus is then relit by the same sun: a cloud matte from the unmixed cloud share, isolated stray puffs dropped, the top of the cloud luminance range pushed toward warm-neutral #FFF4E6 under a soft per-channel shoulder that rolls off near 245, the lower half pulled toward skylight blue (208 degrees, S 0.25), and every edge given a thin translucent fringe of the local sky colour; regrade_towers.py then split-tones every cloud pixel on one smooth logistic key of its log luminance (centred on the 75th percentile, 0.28 stop wide, no hard threshold): warm-neutral #FFF4E6 on the tops, skylight blue 208 degrees (S 0.36) below, at the pixel's own luminance. That key was steep enough to draw the lit tops as pale contour-edged blobs on a grey body, and the clouds sat dim under the film, so cloud_glow.py, the last plate pass, re-develops them: each cloud pixel (the sky matte, with facades taken out of it by their window-grid texture, times the low-saturation weight) comes out from under the plate's shoulder and takes 0.6 stop more light; its log luminance is split by a self-guided filter (about 16 px of the inset) into a large-scale base and a detail layer, and only the base goes through a long filmic shoulder, designed on the screen through a model of the film's own curve: the film as it was up to level 200, then a slope-matched tanh that nears 250 only asymptotically (242 at 1.5 stops past the knee). The detail goes back on top at 1.2x the film's slope at the knee, so the sunlit tops keep their cauliflower cells and crevices instead of piling into a flat-white 244-246 plateau that drew terraced islands at 20 mm. Then it is re-toned on the same logistic key widened to 1.3 stop (centred on the 65th percentile), so lit top to blue shadow is one continuous gradient, and on the lit tops the screen colour itself is set warm (R > G > B by about 5 and 7 levels, toward #FFF4E6) and run back through the film model to the plate, since the film's per-channel shoulder would otherwise bleach plate warmth to neutral. The cloud micro-contrast then grows with the focal length: the inset (all of the 20 to 24 mm frames) is developed for the long end, its detail split off a base filtered over the cloud alone (so the sky never enters it and the cells of a degree or so land in the detail), put back at 2x, over a slower rational shoulder that lets the lit tops shade instead of plateauing; it is developed again as for the wide end (detail 1x, the old shoulder), and the luminance ratio between the two is stored in the inset's alpha, which the engine takes in full at 10 mm and not at all at 24 mm. The matte is unmixed at true coverage, then choked and feathered about 2.5 px round the tower crowns. Stored as scene light / 2, sRGB webp: a 4096 cap to 95 degrees and a native-resolution 4096 inset (the centre of the 8192 cap) of the centre 47.5 degrees, which holds the whole frame at 20 mm.
